note: Only a single system (GOTHOMIS immunisation module, six pilot facilities) and FHIR developer training in June 2024; no exchange between systems is stated.
A funding record saying work strengthens DHIS2 and FHIR-compliant data exchange; it names no exchange between named systems and gives no event date beyond 2021-2026 grant years.

facts.fact: Tanzania's Ministry of Health told The Citizen that 222 public health facilities, from district to national hospitals, are connected to an integrated electronic medical records system introduced in October 2025 that exchanges patient data between facilities through the Health Data Universal API.
facts.system: Health Data Universal API (HDU API) integrated EMR system

systems.tiers: district, regional referral, zonal, specialised and national hospitals

note: Fact dated to the article's published date, the event date not being given beyond the system's introduction in October 2025.

facts.fact: Permanent Secretary Grace Magembe said on 9 September 2026 that the government is preparing a national Health Data Centre to gather and link health information from several sources, and is working to make private-sector and government health systems communicate through interoperability and to reduce the number of digital health systems.
facts.system: Health Data Centre (Kituo cha Taifa cha Takwimu za Afya)

systems.system: Health Data Centre (Kituo cha Taifa cha Takwimu za Afya)

note: No dated exchange between named systems; interoperability is described as a ministry focus and EMR coverage of referral hospitals is a single-system statement. Afya-Tek launched December 2024 is a community system, class other.

facts.fact: Deputy Permanent Secretary Emmanuel Tayari said the government is developing an electronic prescription system linking public and private healthcare providers and plans to integrate patient management systems so medical information can be shared between facilities.

note: Event was the weekend before the 1 September 2026 article, so dated to August 2026 by month.

facts.fact: Minister Mohamed Mchengerwa said at a World Health Assembly side meeting in Geneva that Tanzania has linked more than 45 digital health systems through a national interoperability platform, enabling about 220 health facilities to communicate digitally.
The Minister said more than 45 digital health systems are connected through the national interoperability platform, with about 220 facilities communicating digitally.

note: Study of DHIS2 functionalities in 53 data offices across four countries; it states no exchange between health systems (data integration functionality only noted as lower availability).

facts.fact: The Ministry of Health Permanent Secretary said on 1 October 2025 that for the first time the country has an integrated electronic medical records system linking patient information from community level, health centres and district hospitals to national level.

systems.tiers: community, health centres, district hospitals, national

note: The passages supplied (foreword and acknowledgment) name DHIS2 only as a data source and state nothing on exchange between systems.
